policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'he built it, and covered it, and set up the doors thereof' keeps a singular subject through the clause, matching the qere singular וְיַעֲמִיד; the ketiv plural ויעמידו would require 'they set up'. The verse's only note (Shiloah/Shelah) is classed other and concerns a different word.
ASV text reads 'Baruch the son of Zabbai', which transliterates the ketiv זבי; the mapped textual_variant note 'Another reading is, Zaccai' names the qere זַכַּי as the reading the ASV did not print.
ASV 'After him repaired Hananiah' renders the third-person suffix of the qere אַחֲרָיו; the ketiv אחרי ('after me') would require 'after me'. No note is mapped to this unit.

ASV 'After him repaired Malchijah' renders the third-person suffix of the qere אַחֲרָיו; the ketiv אחרי ('after me') would require 'after me'. The verse's note ('Or, upper chamber') is alternative_rendering on a different word and does not bear on this unit.
